features.summary: Recent changes in the libwebrtc build process focus on improving how the code is managed and integrated. Updates to scripts like `vendor-libwebrtc.py` allow it to be called from other Python programs, which enhances flexibility for developers when working with WebRTC, the technology behind video calls. Additionally, renaming and adjusting the scope of certain variables aims to streamline the build process, making it easier to manage local vendoring of the WebRTC library. These enhancements, including a new Python-based version of a build script, are critical for ensuring faster and more efficient development, contributing to overall performance improvements in Firefox. **Users will benefit indirectly from this smoother development workflow as it can lead to quicker updates and features in their browser.**

features.label: WebRTC web API (RTCPeerConnection)

patches.subject: Start RTCTransportStats.iceState in "new"

patches.author: Byron Campen

patches.subject: Move Maybe<RTCErrorParams> in PeerConnectionImpl DTLS state-change handlers.

patches.author: Sylvestre Ledru
patches.subject: Move Maybe<RTCErrorParams> in MediaTransportChild Recv handlers.

patches.author: Sylvestre Ledru
patches.subject: Move Maybe<RTCErrorParams> in MediaTransportHandlerSTS state-change handlers.

features.summary: Recent updates to the WebRTC web API, which powers real-time communication like video calls, have introduced enhancements to how connection statistics and error handling are managed. The state of ICE (Interactive Connectivity Establishment) will now start in a "new" state, providing clearer insights into the connection's progress, while the DTLS (Datagram Transport Layer Security) role will be initially set to "unknown" until a negotiation occurs. These changes ultimately aim to improve the reliability and transparency of WebRTC connections, making it easier for developers to diagnose issues and ensure smoother communication experiences **without sacrificing security**.

features.label: Connection transport (ICE / DTLS)

patches.author: Byron Campen
patches.subject: Simplify this; alpn was hard-coded anyway.

patches.author: Byron Campen
patches.subject: Handle larger mDNS addresses than we use.

features.summary: Recent updates to the connection transport area of Firefox have resulted in a **simplification of the negotiation process for secure connections** by making adjustments to how Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation (ALPN) is handled, which was previously hard-coded. Additionally, improvements were made to accommodate larger mDNS (Multicast DNS) addresses, enhancing the browser's ability to detect and connect with local network devices. These changes contribute to a more streamlined connection process, improving overall performance and reliability in scenarios where secure communications are essential.

features.label: Negotiation engine (JSEP)

patches.author: Nicolas Grunbaum
patches.subject: Add distinct errors for SDP parsing failures.

patches.author: Sylvestre Ledru
patches.subject: Apply std::move in dom (assorted modules) where values can be moved instead of copied

features.summary: Recent updates to the negotiation engine in Firefox's JSEP (JavaScript Session Establishment Protocol) have improved how the browser handles errors related to SDP (Session Description Protocol) parsing. By introducing distinct error messages for parsing failures, developers can more easily identify and troubleshoot issues that arise during the establishment of multimedia sessions, such as video calls through WebRTC (the technology behind video calls).
